title: KV memory quilting and microstriping eviction policy
creator: Sana Patel
description: Problem: GPU KV cache fragmentation under continuous batching causes elevated memory pressure and uneven slot utilization across model shards. Existing slab/coalescer approaches reduce average fragmentation but struggle with bursty access patterns and cross-batch locality shifts. Goal: design and implement a low-overhead allocation+eviction strategy — called 'memory quilting' with microstriping — that minimizes long-term fragmentation, improves reuse for continuous batching workloads, and gracefully degrades under capacity pressure. The approach stitches small hot regions together at allocation time (quilting) and distributes new allocations across microstrips to avoid creating large holes. Eviction is made eviction-aware by combining batch-aware recency signals, token residency heatmaps, and probabilistic microstrip sampling to keep hot prefixes contiguous when possible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Peak GPU memory fragmentation metric (fragmentation_ratio) reduced by >= 30% on representative continuous-batching trace compared to baseline slab allocator
2) Mean per-token latency impact <= 3% (p99 latency should not regress more than 5ms on our 512-token baseline)
3) End-to-end throughput for steady-state continuous batching improves or remains within 2% of baseline
4) Evictions per minute for heavy-chat workload reduced by >= 25% during 95th percentile load spikes
5) New telemetry (quilting_coalesce_count, microstrip_spread, eviction_rehome_rate) emitted and visible in Console dashboards
6) Feature gated behind runtime flag with safe fallback to current allocator and documented rollout steps
rollout_plan: Feature gated. Stage 1: internal dogfood on non-critical clusters for 48h with sampling enabled (10% traffic). Stage 2: expand to Dedicated CI pools for two weeks, monitor fragmentation_ratio and p99 latency. Stage 3: opt-in beta for customers with high batching workloads. Final: full rollout with automatic fallback if fragmentation_ratio worsens by >10% or p99 latency regresses by >5ms.
test_plan: Unit tests for microstrip allocator invariants and quilting coalescer
Integration test with continuous-batching simulator (replay of production traces)
Chaos test: forced GPU OOM simulation to validate graceful fallback and no-corruption recovery
Performance benchmark harness against existing slab allocator with 3 representative models (Llama-13B, MPT-7B, OpenRWKV-3B)
implementation_steps: 1. Prototype microstrip allocator component (in-memory) and basic quilting heuristic
2. Add eviction-aware sampler that prefers contiguous microstrip rehoming for hot prefixes
3. Integrate with continuous-batching pipeline to surface batch-locality hints to allocator
4. Implement lightweight heatmap telemetry and counters
5. Add runtime feature flag and config knobs (microstrip_width, quilting_threshold, sampler_seed)
6. Run replay-based benchmarks and tune heuristics
7. Create PRs, run CI, and deploy to internal dogfood cluster
8. Observe metrics, iterate, and prepare rollout notes
risks: Increased CPU overhead from quilting/coalesce logic could affect throughput under extreme QPS
Incorrect microstrip sizing may worsen fragmentation if workload distribution shifts unexpectedly
Telemetry gaps could make detecting regressions slow — must ensure metrics emitted before rollout
Edge cases around pinned KV entries and long-lived tokens require careful handling to avoid starvation

notes: Heuristic details: quilting tries to co-allocate nearby slots when a request includes contiguous token prefixes from same session. Microstriping hashes small allocation units across N microstrips to avoid forming large contiguous holes.
Eviction policy: mix of LRU-decay weighted by batch-residency and probabilistic rehome sampling. When rehoming, attempt at most 2 re-homes per eviction to limit CPU cost.
Configuration: start with microstrip_width=4KB, microstrip_count=64, quilting_threshold=0.6 (coalesce if adjacent free fraction > 60%). Tunable via runtime config.
Related work: compare against 'shadow-harmonizer' and 'slot-orchestra' experiments (ENG-413207, ENG-908123) to understand interactions.
